hero.lead: A nation of 1.4 million on the Baltic with forest across almost six tenths of its land and public debt of 24.0% of GDP.

capital.heading: Low debt and strong schools, and a living income for all.

register.name: Ten-year government bond (Republic of Estonia 3.5% 2036)
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · issued 7 May 2026 · settled 14 May 2026 · due 14 May 2036 · coupon 3.5% · yield 3.609% · mid-swaps +60 basis points
register.note: Orders of more than €2.2 billion from 90 investors; arranged by DZ Bank, HSBC and J.P. Morgan
register.text: A ten-year bond of €1 billion issued by the Republic of Estonia at a price of 99.098, with a coupon of 3.5% and a yield to maturity of 3.609%. Asset managers bought 54% and commercial banks 18%. It sets the cost at which the state itself borrows for ten years, the reference for long-term financing of the seven standards.

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: European Commission · Recovery and Resilience Facility · grants €953M, no loans · Council implementing decision of 29 October 2021 · REPowerEU chapter added 16 June 2023 · Commission decision of 21 September 2026 authorising an instalment
register.note: The final payment request, of €190.6 million, was positively assessed on 10 November 2026, as The Brussels Times reports; all milestones and targets were due by August 2026
register.text: EU grants under NextGenerationEU for reforms and investments agreed with Estonia, paid in instalments against milestones and targets; 59% of the plan supports climate objectives. Its measures include €72 million to improve access to health care, the energy-efficient renovation of 3,500 dwellings (€75 million) and €10 million to strengthen social resilience, which serve the health, shelter, energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Green investment programme of the City of Tartu
register.detail: European Investment Bank · announced by the City of Tartu, 9 September 2026 · programme to 2030 · energy-efficient renovation of schools, kindergartens and municipal buildings · cycling and pedestrian routes
register.note: The city’s announcement does not give the date of signature or the term of the loan
register.text: An EIB loan to the City of Tartu for an investment programme that runs to 2030. It finances the energy-efficient renovation of schools, kindergartens and other municipal buildings and the upgrade of cycling and pedestrian routes; the schools serve the education standard and the renovation the energy standard.

register.name: Tallinn Sustainable Infrastructure II (framework loan)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · project 20240050 · approved 19 December 2025 · signed 18 June 2026 · announced 22 June 2026 · investment programme to 2030 · total cost about €278M
register.note: The loan covers 45% of the programme; about 58% of the investment is projected to serve climate and environmental goals
register.text: A framework loan to the City of Tallinn, home to about 460,000 people, which the city allocates across projects as they are prepared. It focuses on the rehabilitation and upgrade of public buildings, notably schools and social housing, with energy efficiency, parks, streets and cycling paths; the schools serve the education standard and the social housing the shelter standard.

register.name: InvestEU risk sharing with Enterprise Estonia
register.detail: European Investment Fund · InvestEU programme · announced 20 June 2025 · loans and guarantees of the Estonian Business and Innovation Agency (EIS)
register.note: Financing unlocked for SMEs and microbusinesses, including green investments
register.text: An agreement under the InvestEU programme in which the EIF shares the risk of the loans and guarantees offered by Enterprise Estonia (EIS), unlocking €109 million in financing for Estonian small and micro businesses. Affordable credit for small firms serves the livelihood standard, the one furthest from reach.

register.name: Cohesion policy, 2021–2027
register.detail: European Commission · Partnership Agreement adopted 18 July 2022 · European Social Fund Plus €534M · Just Transition Fund €354M
register.note: The European Social Fund Plus money also addresses child poverty and supports long-term care reform
register.text: EU cohesion policy funding for Estonia’s economic, social and territorial cohesion in 2021–2027. The European Social Fund Plus share addresses social, health, lifelong learning and labour market needs and child poverty, and the Just Transition Fund helps Estonia’s transition; they serve the livelihood, education and health standards.

register.name: Inaugural green bond of Eesti Energia
register.detail: European Investment Bank · announced 1 June 2026 · €300M five-year green bond · fixed coupon · the EIB’s first investment in a green senior bond in the Baltic region
register.note: The EIB’s share of the €300 million issue
register.text: The EIB committed €20 million to the first green bond of Eesti Energia, a €300 million five-year issue. Its proceeds finance renewable energy generation, electricity networks that integrate more renewables, battery storage and electric vehicle charging, which serve the energy standard with clean power.

register.name: Gren Group energy infrastructure in the Baltics
register.detail: Nordic Investment Bank · 7-year loan · announced 5 May 2026 · option to increase by €15M · Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania
register.note: Shared across the three Baltic states; the share for Estonia is not given
register.text: A seven-year NIB loan to Gren Group, an energy infrastructure platform in Northern Europe, for district heating and cooling networks, combined heat and power, renewable heat and battery storage in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. It serves the energy standard with heat for homes.

register.name: Synthetic securitisation with Coop Pank
register.detail: European Investment Bank and European Investment Fund · announced December 2025 · frees capital for lending to SMEs and mid-caps through 2028
register.note: New lending capacity of up to €249 million, not a loan of that amount
register.text: A synthetic securitisation supported by the EIB and the EIF that frees capital at Coop Pank, an Estonian bank, for up to €249 million of new lending to small and medium-sized firms and mid-caps through 2028. Credit for small firms serves the livelihood standard, the one furthest from reach.

register.name: Tallinn wastewater modernisation (AS Tallinna Vesi)
register.detail: Nordic Investment Bank · loan dated 27 November 2025 · announced 11 December 2025 · extends the 2023–2025 project financing through 2026
register.note: About 18 km of outdated wastewater networks to be renovated
register.text: A NIB loan to AS Tallinna Vesi, the utility that serves around 500,000 people in Tallinn and its surrounding areas, to replace wastewater assets, renovate about 18 km of outdated networks, upgrade the treatment plant and expand the stormwater system. It serves the water and shelter standards with safe wastewater treatment.

register.name: Battery energy storage parks Hertz 1 and Hertz 2
register.detail: Nordic Investment Bank · 10-year loan · announced 30 October 2025 · Kiisa and Aruküla, about 25 km from Tallinn · 200 MW and 400 MWh · InvestEU
register.note: To Baltic Storage Platform OÜ, a joint venture of Evecon, Corsica Sole and Mirova; the EBRD also finances the project
register.text: A ten-year NIB loan to Baltic Storage Platform OÜ for two battery energy storage parks near Tallinn, together 200 MW of power and 400 MWh of storage, supported by the InvestEU programme. Storage steadies a grid that takes more wind and solar power, which serves the energy standard.

register.name: Risti solar park (244 MW)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · loan to Sunly in 2025 · in the EIB Group’s results for Estonia, 29 January 2026
register.note: The release does not give the date of signature or the term
register.text: An EIB loan to Sunly for the 244 MW Risti solar park, part of the €336 million of EIB Group financing in Estonia in 2025. It serves the energy standard with clean power.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.
items.alt: Pine and birch forest in Estonia at sunrise, with a mossy floor and a bog pool beyond the trees.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 15.3% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: The cobbled square of Tallinn’s medieval Old Town in Estonia at sunset, with colourful gabled houses, café terraces and people seen only at a distance.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.
items.alt: Wind turbines and power lines across flat coastal grassland and pine woods in western Estonia, with the Baltic Sea on the horizon.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.
items.alt: Yellow rapeseed and golden barley fields around a wooden farmstead in Estonia at sunset, with forest beyond.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.
items.alt: A calm forest lake in Estonia with reeds, pine and birch on the shore and a small wooden jetty.

items.name: Maarja Küla
items.text: A community in Kiidjärve, Põlva County, run by the Maarja Küla foundation, where adults with intellectual disabilities live, work and grow together, with daily workshops in wood, clay, gardening and art; it has hosted volunteers from more than fifteen countries since 2004.

items.name: Eesti Toidupank (Estonian Food Bank)
items.text: A food bank with the longest history and the largest network for passing donated edible food to people in need in Estonia: in 2025 it distributed about four million kilograms of food, and its food aid reaches more than 15,000 people every week.

items.name: FudLoop
items.text: A venture that recovers surplus food from shops and wholesalers before it is thrown away and stocks food lockers in Tallinn, which its users open for a monthly fee.

items.name: Peaasjad (Peaasi.ee)
items.text: A non-profit that runs Peaasi.ee, a mental health portal for young people with e-counselling and youth counselling, and teaches mental health first aid in trainings, including for companies.

items.name: Uuskasutuskeskus (Reuse Centre)
items.text: An independent social enterprise founded in 2004 that puts used clothes, furniture, household appliances and other goods back into circulation through its reuse shops, and with charity partners donates to people in need the things they ask for.
